what: the contract between the OpenSearch Dashboards front end and the server behind it, read out of a running one. Regenerate with tools/osd_pin.py rather than editing.

accessibility:disableAnimations.name: Disable Animations
accessibility:disableAnimations.description: Turn off all unnecessary animations in the OpenSearch Dashboards UI. Refresh the page to apply the changes.

dateFormat.name: Date format
dateFormat.description: When displaying a pretty formatted date, use this format

dateFormat:tz.name: Timezone for date formatting
dateFormat:tz.description: Which timezone should be used. "Browser" will use the timezone detected by your browser.

dateFormat:scaled.name: Scaled date format
dateFormat:scaled.description: Values that define the format used in situations where time-based data is rendered in order, and formatted timestamps should adapt to the interval between measurements. Keys are ISO8601 intervals.

dateFormat:dow.name: Day of week
dateFormat:dow.description: What day should weeks start on?

dateNanosFormat.name: Date with nanoseconds format
dateNanosFormat.description: Used for the date_nanos datatype of OpenSearch

truncate:maxHeight.name: Maximum table cell height
truncate:maxHeight.description: The maximum height that a cell in a table should occupy. Set to 0 to disable truncation

defaultRoute.name: Default route
defaultRoute.description: This setting specifies the default route when opening OpenSearch Dashboards, You can use this setting to modify the landing page when opening OpenSearch Dashboards, The route must be a relative URL.

notifications:banner.name: Custom banner notification
notifications:banner.description: A custom banner intended for temporary notices to all users. Markdown supported.

notifications:lifetime:banner.name: Banner notification lifetime
notifications:lifetime:banner.description: The time in milliseconds which a banner notification will be displayed on-screen for. Setting to Infinity will disable the countdown.

notifications:lifetime:error.name: Error notification lifetime
notifications:lifetime:error.description: The time in milliseconds which an error notification will be displayed on-screen for. Setting to Infinity will disable.

notifications:lifetime:warning.name: Warning notification lifetime
notifications:lifetime:warning.description: The time in milliseconds which a warning notification will be displayed on-screen for. Setting to Infinity will disable.

notifications:lifetime:info.name: Info notification lifetime
notifications:lifetime:info.description: The time in milliseconds which an information notification will be displayed on-screen for. Setting to Infinity will disable.

theme:enableUserControl.name: Enable user control
theme:enableUserControl.description: Enable users to control theming and dark or light mode via "Appearance" control in top navigation. When true, those settings can no longer be set globally by administrators.

theme:darkMode.name: Dark mode
theme:darkMode.description: Enable a dark mode for the OpenSearch Dashboards UI. A page refresh is required for the setting to be applied.

theme:version.name: Theme version
theme:version.description:
Switch between the themes used for the current and next versions of OpenSearch Dashboards. A page refresh is required for the setting to be applied.

Theme feedback

state:storeInSessionStorage.name: Store URLs in session storage
state:storeInSessionStorage.description: The URL can sometimes grow to be too large for some browsers to handle. To counter-act this we are testing if storing parts of the URL in session storage could help. Please let us know how it goes!

enableAIFeatures.name: Enable AI features
enableAIFeatures.description: The setting to enable all AI-powered features in OpenSearch Dashboards.

visualization:tileMap:maxPrecision.name: Maximum tile map precision
visualization:tileMap:maxPrecision.description: The maximum geoHash precision displayed on tile maps: 7 is high, 10 is very high, 12 is the max. Explanation of cell dimensions

visualization:tileMap:WMSdefaults.name: Default WMS properties
visualization:tileMap:WMSdefaults.description: Default properties for the WMS map server support in the coordinate map

csv:separator.name: CSV separator
csv:separator.description: Separate exported values with this string

csv:quoteValues.name: Quote CSV values
csv:quoteValues.description: Should values be quoted in csv exports?

metaFields.name: Meta fields
metaFields.description: Fields that exist outside of _source to merge into our document when displaying it

doc_table:highlight.name: Highlight results
doc_table:highlight.description: Highlight results in Discover and Saved Searches Dashboard. Highlighting makes requests slow when working on big documents.

query:queryString:options.name: Query string options
query:queryString:options.description: Options for the lucene query string parser. Is only used when "Query language" is set to Lucene.

query:allowLeadingWildcards.name: Allow leading wildcards in query
query:allowLeadingWildcards.description: When set, * is allowed as the first character in a query clause. Currently only applies when experimental query features are enabled in the query bar. To disallow leading wildcards in basic lucene queries, use query:queryString:options.

search:queryLanguage.name: Query language
search:queryLanguage.description: Query language used by the query bar. DQL is a new language built specifically for OpenSearch Dashboards.

sort:options.name: Sort options
sort:options.description: Options for the OpenSearch sort parameter

defaultIndex.name: Default index
defaultIndex.description: The index to access if no index is set

courier:ignoreFilterIfFieldNotInIndex.name: Ignore filter(s)
courier:ignoreFilterIfFieldNotInIndex.description: This configuration enhances support for dashboards containing visualizations accessing dissimilar indexes. When disabled, all filters are applied to all visualizations. When enabled, filter(s) will be ignored for a visualization when the visualization's index does not contain the filtering field.

courier:setRequestPreference.name: Request preference
courier:setRequestPreference.description:
Allows you to set which shards handle your search requests.
  • Session ID: restricts operations to execute all search requests on the same shards. This has the benefit of reusing shard caches across requests.
  • Custom: allows you to define a your own preference. Use 'courier:customRequestPreference' to customize your preference value.
  • None: means do not set a preference. This might provide better performance because requests can be spread across all shard copies. However, results might be inconsistent because different shards might be in different refresh states.

courier:customRequestPreference.name: Custom request preference
courier:customRequestPreference.description: Request Preference used when courier:setRequestPreference is set to "custom".

courier:maxConcurrentShardRequests.name: Max Concurrent Shard Requests
courier:maxConcurrentShardRequests.description: Controls the max_concurrent_shard_requests setting used for _msearch requests sent by OpenSearch Dashboards. Set to 0 to disable this config and use the OpenSearch default.

courier:batchSearches.name: Batch concurrent searches
courier:batchSearches.description:
When disabled, dashboard panels will load individually, and search requests will terminate when users navigate
           away or update the query. When enabled, dashboard panels will load together when all of the data is loaded, and
           searches will not terminate.

search:includeFrozen.name: Search in frozen indices
search:includeFrozen.description: Will include frozen indices in results if enabled. Searching through frozen indices might increase the search time.

histogram:barTarget.name: Target bars
histogram:barTarget.description: Attempt to generate around this many bars when using "auto" interval in date histograms

histogram:maxBars.name: Maximum bars
histogram:maxBars.description: Never show more than this many bars in date histograms, scale values if needed

history:limit.name: History limit
history:limit.description: In fields that have history (e.g. query inputs), show this many recent values

shortDots:enable.name: Shorten fields
shortDots:enable.description: Shorten long fields, for example, instead of foo.bar.baz, show f.b.baz

format:defaultTypeMap.name: Field type format name
format:defaultTypeMap.description: Map of the format name to use by default for each field type. "_default_" is used if the field type is not mentioned explicitly

format:number:defaultPattern.name: Number format
format:number:defaultPattern.description: Default numeral format for the "number" format

format:percent:defaultPattern.name: Percent format
format:percent:defaultPattern.description: Default numeral format for the "percent" format

format:bytes:defaultPattern.name: Bytes format
format:bytes:defaultPattern.description: Default numeral format for the "bytes" format

format:currency:defaultPattern.name: Currency format
format:currency:defaultPattern.description: Default numeral format for the "currency" format

format:number:defaultLocale.name: Formatting locale
format:number:defaultLocale.description: Numeral language locale

data:withLongNumerals.name: Extend Numeric Precision
data:withLongNumerals.description: Turn on for precise handling of extremely large numbers. Turn off to optimize performance when high precision for large values isn't required.

timepicker:refreshIntervalDefaults.name: Time filter refresh interval
timepicker:refreshIntervalDefaults.description: The timefilter's default refresh interval. The "value" needs to be specified in milliseconds.

timepicker:timeDefaults.name: Time filter defaults
timepicker:timeDefaults.description: The timefilter selection to use when OpenSearch Dashboards is started without one

timepicker:quickRanges.name: Time filter quick ranges
timepicker:quickRanges.description: The list of ranges to show in the Quick section of the time filter. This should be an array of objects, with each object containing "from", "to" (see accepted formats), and "display" (the title to be displayed).

indexPattern:placeholder.name: Index pattern placeholder
indexPattern:placeholder.description: The placeholder for the "Index pattern name" field in "Management > Index Patterns > Create Index Pattern".

filters:pinnedByDefault.name: Pin filters by default
filters:pinnedByDefault.description: Whether the filters should have a global state (be pinned) by default

filterEditor:suggestValues.name: Filter editor suggest values
filterEditor:suggestValues.description: Set this property to false to prevent the filter editor from suggesting values for fields.

query:enhancements:enabled.name: Enable query enhancements
query:enhancements:enabled.description: Experimental: Allows users to query data using enhancements where available. If disabled, only querying and querying languages that are considered production-ready are available to the user.

query:enhancements:suggestValues.name: Allow for Value Suggestion through the enhancements APIs
query:enhancements:suggestValues.description: Value Suggestion will be done through a SQL query to the enhancements APIs, sorted by the most frequent options Experimental: Requires query enhancements enabled.

query:enhancements:suggestValuesLimit.name: Enhancements Value Suggestion Limit
query:enhancements:suggestValuesLimit.description: The limit on number of values fetched Experimental: Requires query enhancements enabled.

query:dataframe:hydrationStrategy.name: Data frame hydration strategy
query:dataframe:hydrationStrategy.description:
Allows you to set how often the data frame schema is updated.
  • On data source change: hydrates the schema when the data source changes. For example, any time the index pattern is change the data frame schema is hydrated.
  • Per query: hydrates the schema per query to the data source. Could be expensive, but ensures the schema of the data frame fits the result set.
  • Per response: hydrates the schema if the data source returns a schema. Not Implemented.
  • Advanced: hydrates the schema in intervals. If the schema hasn't changed the interval increases. If the schema has changed the interval resets. Not Implemented.
Experimental: Requires query enhancements enabled.

search:queryLanguageBlocklist.name: Additional query languages blocklist
search:queryLanguageBlocklist.description: Additional languages that are blocked from being used in the query editor. Note: DQL and Lucene will not be blocked even if set.

search:includeAllFields.name: Include all fields in search request
search:includeAllFields.description: Experimental: Adds the "fields": ["*"] property to search request body

savedObjects:perPage.name: Objects per page
savedObjects:perPage.description: Number of objects to show per page in the load dialog

savedObjects:listingLimit.name: Objects listing limit
savedObjects:listingLimit.description: Number of objects to fetch for the listing pages

searchWorkspace:dismissGetStarted.description: Dismiss get started section on search overview page

visualize:enableLabs.name: Enable experimental visualizations
visualize:enableLabs.description:
Allows users to create, view, and edit experimental visualizations. If disabled,
            only visualizations that are considered production-ready are available to the user.

visualize:disableBucketAgg.name: Disable visualizations bucket aggregation types
visualize:disableBucketAgg.description:
A comma-separated list of bucket aggregations' names. e.g. significant_terms, terms.
            Deactivates the specified bucket aggregations from visualizations.

timeline:es.timefield.name: Time field
timeline:es.timefield.description: Default field containing a timestamp when using .opensearch()

timeline:es.default_index.name: Default index
timeline:es.default_index.description: Default opensearch index to search with .opensearch()

timeline:target_buckets.name: Target buckets
timeline:target_buckets.description: The number of buckets to shoot for when using auto intervals

timeline:max_buckets.name: Maximum buckets
timeline:max_buckets.description: The maximum number of buckets a single datasource can return

timeline:min_interval.name: Minimum interval
timeline:min_interval.description: The smallest interval that will be calculated when using "auto"

timeline:graphite.url.name: Graphite URL
timeline:graphite.url.description: [experimental] The URL of your graphite host

visbuilder:enableVega.name: Enable vega transformation in visbuilder
visbuilder:enableVega.description: Allow visbuilder to render visualizations via vega.

visualization:enablePluginAugmentation.name: Enable plugin augmentation
visualization:enablePluginAugmentation.description: Plugin functionality can be accessed from line chart visualizations

visualization:enablePluginAugmentation.m.name: Max number of associated augmentations
visualization:enablePluginAugmentation.m.description: Associating more than 10 plugin resources per visualization can lead to performance issues and increase the cost of running clusters.

visualization:regionmap:showWarnings.name: Show region map warning
visualization:regionmap:showWarnings.description: Whether the region map shows a warning when terms cannot be joined to a shape on the map.

visualization:regionmap:customVectorMapM.name: Custom vector map size
visualization:regionmap:customVectorMapM.description: The maximum number of features to load from custom vector map. A higher number might have negative impact on browser rendering performance.

search-relevance:experimental_workbench_.name: Experimental Search Relevance Workbench
search-relevance:experimental_workbench_.description: Whether to opt-in the experimental search relevance workbench feature

reporting:useOcr.name: Reporting use OCR on PDF
reporting:useOcr.description: Whether to run optical character recognition on PDF reports to make text selectable

reporting:useFOR.name: Reporting use ForeignObject rendering
reporting:useFOR.description: Whether to use ForeignObject rendering when generating reports. If it causes issues, try disabling this option.

visualization:colorMapping.name: Color mapping
visualization:colorMapping.description: Maps values to specified colors within visualizations

observability:traceAnalyticsSpanIndices.name: Trace analytics span indices
observability:traceAnalyticsSpanIndices.description: Configure span indices that adhere to Data Prepper schema, to be used by the trace analytics plugin

observability:traceAnalyticsServiceIndic.name: Trace analytics service indices
observability:traceAnalyticsServiceIndic.description: Configure service indices that adhere to Data Prepper schema, to be used by the trace analytics plugin

observability:traceAnalyticsCustomModeDe.name: Trace analytics default mode
observability:traceAnalyticsCustomModeDe.description: Enable this to default to Data Prepper mode in the trace analytics plugin

observability:traceAnalyticsCorrelatedLo.name: Trace analytics correlated logs indices
observability:traceAnalyticsCorrelatedLo.description: Configure correlated logs indices, to be used by the trace analytics plugin to correlate spans and services to logs

observability:traceAnalyticsCorrelatedLo.name: Trace analytics correlated logs fields
observability:traceAnalyticsCorrelatedLo.description: Configure correlated logs fields, to be used by the trace analytics plugin for correlate spans and services to logs

observability:defaultDashboard.name: Observability default dashboard
observability:defaultDashboard.description: The default dashboard to display in Observability overview page

observability:overviewCardsDisplay.name: Observability overview cards
observability:overviewCardsDisplay.description: Show the Observability overview page cards

metrics:max_buckets.name: Maximum buckets
metrics:max_buckets.description: The maximum number of buckets a single datasource can return

visualization:dimmingOpacity.name: Dimming opacity
visualization:dimmingOpacity.description: The opacity of the chart items that are dimmed when highlighting another element of the chart. The lower this number, the more the highlighted element will stand out. This must be a number between 0 and 1.

visualization:heatmap:maxBuckets.name: Heatmap maximum buckets
visualization:heatmap:maxBuckets.description: The maximum number of buckets a single datasource can return. A higher number might have negative impact on browser rendering performance

defaultColumns.name: Default columns
defaultColumns.description: Columns displayed by default in the Discovery tab

discover:sampleSize.name: Number of rows
discover:sampleSize.description: The number of rows to show in the table

discover:aggs:terms:size.name: Number of terms
discover:aggs:terms:size.description: Determines how many terms will be visualized when clicking the "visualize" button, in the field drop downs, in the discover sidebar.

discover:sort:defaultOrder.name: Default sort direction
discover:sort:defaultOrder.description: Controls the default sort direction for time based index patterns in the Discover app.

discover:searchOnPageLoad.name: Search on page load
discover:searchOnPageLoad.description: Controls whether a search is executed when Discover first loads. This setting does not have an effect when loading a saved search.

doc_table:hideTimeColumn.name: Hide 'Time' column
doc_table:hideTimeColumn.description: Hide the 'Time' column in Discover and in all Saved Searches on Dashboards.

fields:popularLimit.name: Popular fields limit
fields:popularLimit.description: The top N most popular fields to show

context:defaultSize.name: Context size
context:defaultSize.description: The number of surrounding entries to show in the context view

context:step.name: Context size step
context:step.description: The step size to increment or decrement the context size by

context:tieBreakerFields.name: Tie breaker fields
context:tieBreakerFields.description: A comma-separated list of fields to use for tie-breaking between documents that have the same timestamp value. From this list the first field that is present and sortable in the current index pattern is used.

discover:modifyColumnsOnSwitch.name: Modify columns when changing index patterns
discover:modifyColumnsOnSwitch.description: Remove columns that not available in the new index pattern.

            padding: 0;
            border: none;
            vertical-align: baseline;
          }

          body, html {
            width: 100%;
            height: 100%;
            margin: 0;
            display: block;
          }

          {/* used on loading page */}
          .osdWelcomeView {
            line-height: 1.5;
            height: 100%;
            display: -webkit-box;
            display: -webkit-flex;
            display: -ms-flexbox;
            display: flex;
            -webkit-box-flex: 1;
            -webkit-flex: 1 0 auto;
                -ms-flex: 1 0 auto;
                    flex: 1 0 auto;
            -webkit-box-orient: vertical;
            -webkit-box-direction: normal;
            -webkit-flex-direction: column;
                -ms-flex-direction: column;
                    flex-direction: column;
            -webkit-box-align: center;

                    align-items: center;
            -webkit-box-pack: center;
            -webkit-justify-content: center;
                -ms-flex-pack: center;
                    justify-content: center;
          }

          .legacyBrowserErrorLogo {
            height: 64px;
          }

          .osdWelcomeTitle {
            font-size: 20px;
            margin: 16px 0;
            animation: fadeIn 1s ease-in-out;
            animation-fill-mode: forwards;
            opacity: 0;
            animation-delay: 1.0s;
          }

          .osdWelcomeText {
            display: inline-block;
            font-size: 14px;
            line-height: 40px !important;
            height: 40px !important;
          }

          .osdLoaderWrap {
            text-align: center;
            line-height: 1;
            text-align: center;
            letter-spacing: -.005em;
            -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%;
            -ms-text-size-adjust: 100%;
            font-kerning: normal;
            font-weight: 400;
          }

          .osdLoaderWrap svg {
            width: 64px;
            height: 64px;
            margin: auto;
            line-height: 1;
          }

          .osdLoader path {
            stroke: white;
          }

          .osdProgress {
            display: inline-block;
            position: relative;
            width: 32px;
            height: 4px;
            overflow: hidden;
            line-height: 1;
          }

          .osdProgress:before {
            position: absolute;
            content: '';
            height: 4px;
            width: 100%;
            top: 0;
            bottom: 0;
            left: 0;
            transform: scaleX(0) translateX(0%);
            animation: osdProgress 1s cubic-bezier(.694, .0482, .335, 1) infinite;
          }

          .loadingLogoContainer {
            height: 80px;
            padding: 8px;
          }

          .loadingLogo {
            height: 100%;
            max-width: 100%;
          }

          .darkOnly, .lightOnly {
            display: none;
          }

          @keyframes osdProgress {
            0% {
              transform: scaleX(1) translateX(-100%);
            }

            100% {
              transform: scaleX(1) translateX(100%);
            }
          }

tutorials.name: APM
tutorials.shortDescription: Collect in-depth performance metrics and errors from inside your applications.
tutorials.longDescription: Application Performance Monitoring (APM) collects in-depth performance metrics and errors from inside your application. It allows you to monitor the performance of thousands of applications in real time. [Learn more]({config.docs.base_url}guide/en/apm/get-started/{config.docs.version}/index.html).

instructions.title: Download and unpack APM Server
instructions.textPre:
1. Download the APM Server Windows zip file from the [Download page](https://opensearch.org/downloads/apm/apm-server).
2. Extract the contents of the zip file into `C:\Program Files`.
3. Rename the `apm-server-{config.opensearchDashboards.version}-windows` directory to `APM-Server`.
4. Open a PowerShell prompt as an Administrator (right-click the PowerShell icon and select **Run As Administrator**). If you are running Windows XP, you might need to download and install PowerShell.
5. From the PowerShell prompt, run the following commands to install APM Server as a Windows service:
instructions.textPost: Note: If script execution is disabled on your system, you need to set the execution policy for the current session to allow the script to run. For example: `PowerShell.exe -ExecutionPolicy UnRestricted -File .\install-service-apm-server.ps1`.

instructions.title: Download the APM agent
instructions.textPre: Download the agent jar from [Maven Central](http://search.maven.org/#search%7Cga%7C1%7Ca%3Aelastic-apm-agent). Do **not** add the agent as a dependency to your application.

instructions.title: Start your application with the javaagent flag
instructions.textPre:
Add the `-javaagent` flag and configure the agent with system properties.

 * Set required service name (allowed characters: a-z, A-Z, 0-9, -, _, and space)
 * Set custom APM Server URL (default: http://localhost:8200)
 * Set the base package of your application
instructions.textPost: See the [documentation]({config.docs.base_url}guide/en/apm/agent/java/current/index.html) for configuration options and advanced usage.

instructions.title: Enable Real User Monitoring support in APM Server
instructions.textPre: APM Server disables RUM support by default. See the [documentation]({config.docs.base_url}guide/en/apm/server/{config.docs.version}/configuration-rum.html) for details on how to enable RUM support.

instructions.title: Set up the Agent as a dependency
instructions.textPre:
You can install the Agent as a dependency to your application with `npm install @elastic/apm-rum --save`.

The Agent can then be initialized and configured in your application like this:
commands: // Set required service name (allowed characters: a-z, A-Z, 0-9, -, _, and space)
// Set custom APM Server URL (default: http://localhost:8200)
// Set service version (required for source map feature)
instructions.textPost: Framework integrations, like React or Angular, have custom dependencies. See the [integration documentation]({config.docs.base_url}guide/en/apm/agent/rum-js/current/framework-integrations.html) for more information.

instructions.title: Set up the Agent with Script Tags
instructions.textPre: Alternatively, you can use Script tags to set up and configure the Agent. Add a `<script>` tag to the HTML page and use the `elasticApm` global object to load and initialize the agent. Don't forget to download the latest version of the RUM Agent from [GitHub](https://github.com/elastic/apm-agent-rum-js/releases/latest) or [UNPKG](https://unpkg.com/@elastic/apm-rum/dist/bundles/elastic-apm-rum.umd.min.js), and host the file on your Server/CDN before deploying to production.

instructions.textPre: Instrument your Go application by using one of the provided instrumentation modules or by using the tracer API directly.

instructions.title: Download the APM agent
instructions.textPre:
Add the agent package(s) from [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages?q=Elastic.apm) to your .NET application. There are multiple       NuGet packages available for different use cases. 

For an ASP.NET Core application with Entity Framework       Core download the [Elastic.Apm.NetCoreAll](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Elastic.Apm.NetCoreAll) package. This package will automatically add every       agent component to your application. 

 In case you would like to to minimize the dependencies, you can use the       [Elastic.Apm.AspNetCore](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Elastic.Apm.AspNetCore) package for just       ASP.NET Core monitoring or the [Elastic.Apm.EfCore](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Elastic.Apm.EntityFrameworkCore) package for just Entity Framework Core monitoring. 

       In case you only want to use the public Agent API for manual instrumentation use the [Elastic.Apm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Elastic.Apm) package.

instructions.title: Add the agent to the application
instructions.textPre: In case of ASP.NET Core with the `Elastic.Apm.NetCoreAll` package, call the `UseAllElasticApm`       method in the `Configure` method within the `Startup.cs` file.
commands: public void Configure(IApplicationBuilder app, IHostingEnvironment env)
instructions.textPost: Passing an `IConfiguration` instance is optional and by doing so, the agent will read config settings through this       `IConfiguration` instance (e.g. from the `appsettings.json` file).

instructions.title: Sample appsettings.json file:
commands: "ServiceName" : "MyApp", //allowed characters: a-z, A-Z, 0-9, -, _, and space. Default is the entry assembly of the application
instructions.textPost:
In case you don’t pass an `IConfiguration` instance to the agent (e.g. in case of non ASP.NET Core applications)       you can also configure the agent through environment variables. 
       See [the documentation]({config.docs.base_url}guide/en/apm/agent/dotnet/current/configuration.html) for advanced usage.
